programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha Fuigheag a’ cluich le rudeigin beag spòrsail a lorg e. Feumaidh Boban obrachadh a-mach cò às a thàinig an rud agus an uairsin a thilleadh air ais. Fuigheag is playing with something he’s found. Boban must work out where the item has come from and return it.

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid agus a caraidean a’ dèanamh bonnaich-èisg bhlasta. Linda and her friends make tasty fishcakes.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Nìp a’ lorg chuibhlichean. Tha Tilidh a’ lorg chuibhlichean. Mu dheireadh thall, tha Àtaidh a’ lorg chuibhlichean dha fhèin. Chan eil iad cho cumhachdach an toiseach, ach chan fhada gus am fàs iad ro chumhachdach fiù ’s! Neep and Teal find some wheels. Finally, Abney gets hold of some wheels of his own. They aren't brilliant at first, but soon they become perhaps even a bit too brilliant!

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: An-diugh, tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean a’ coinneachadh ri losgann is cinn-pholla bheaga. Today, Ladybird and Bee meet a frog and some small tadpoles.

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Nuair a chluinneas Comhachag Sionnach a’ bruidhinn mu Mhaigheach mar a’ charaid as fheàrr a th’ aige, tha Comhachag ag iarraidh a’ cheart rud air a shon fhèin. Aon mhadainn, tha balùn dearg a’ nochdadh ri taobh na craoibhe aige. Seo a’ charaid as fheàrr aig Comhachag! Tha iad a’ dèanamh a h-uile rud còmhla gus an tòiseach am balùn ri searg. Tha Comhachag troimhe chèile. Ciamar idir a thogas Sionnach agus Maigheach a shunnd? When Fox mentions that Hare is his best friend, Owl decides that he needs a best friend, too. One morning, a red balloon suddenly appears near his tree. This is Owl’s new best friend! They do everything together, but then the balloon slowly starts to deflate. Owl is in despair. What can Fox and Hare do to cheer Owl up again?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Pàdruig Moireasdan a’ leughadh An Latha Spòrs. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Nick Butterworth agus Mick Inkpen. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Pàdruig Morrison reads An Latha Spòrs, written and illustrated by Nick Butterworth and Mick Inkpen, and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: Stri
programme.desc: Tha preasantairean CBBC ALBA uabhasach fhèin measail air dùbhlain ach saoil cò shoirbhicheas is Rachel a’ tadhal orra? The CBBC ALBA presenters love a good challenge but who will emerge victorious as Rachel joins them?

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Pòl agus a charaidean a’ dol air turas-sgoile suas an canàl is tha iad a’ dùsgadh seann uilebheist air a bheil An Liobach Mòr. Tha An Liobach Mòr gam putadh thairis air eas, is tha seo gan tilgeil air ais ann an ùine gu àm Diùrasach. Dave and his friends embark on a school trip along the canal, where they awaken an ancient monster called Big Lippy. The beast pushes them over a waterfall and sends them back in time, to the Jurassic era.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Pòl a’ lorg seann chonsail geama coimpiutair aig an dump. Sa gheama feumar sombaidhean a spreadhadh, is tha a charaid, Ceitidh Sombaidh, ga ghabhail san t-sròin. Tha Ceitidh a’ dol às a dhèidh le buidheann de shombaidhean mòr fìor is fiadhaich. Dave finds a handheld computer game at the dump. The game involves killing zombies which his friend, Zombie Katie, finds rather insulting. Exacting her revenge, Dave finds himself confronted with a group of very angry and very real zombies.

programme.title: Na Speuran
programme.desc: Thèid air turas suas dha na speuran cuide ris an Speuradair Zach! Air an turas fànais iongantach seo tha e ag innse dhuinn mu Theileasgop Sheumais Webb. Bidh e cuideachd a’ beachdachadh air a’ cheist mhòr “a bheil sìon beò air planaidean eile?” Blast off into space with Astronaut Zach! In this amazing space voyage, he tells us about the James Webb Telescope and also debates the age-old question: 'Is there life on other planets?'

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Anns an leabhar-lann, tha an leabhraiche feumach air taic bho Hilda is Flòraidh nuair a tha iad a' tighinn tarsainn air Tùr nam Bana-bhuidseach, is nuair a tha aca ri rèiseadh an aghaidh tìm airson leabhar a tha a dhìth a lorg. The librarian needs Hilda and Flòraidh’s help as they come across the Witches Tower, and when they have to race against time to find a missing book.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra
programme.desc: Mairi travels to Logan Botanic Garden, Scotland’s most exotic garden! Curator Richard Baines shows Mairi some of the many plants that can be grown outdoors at Logan that would need to be kept indoors anywhere else in Scotland. They make their way through the giant Gunnera Bog, before enjoying some mocktails made with plants selected from the garden. Tèarlach Quinnell talks about the various ways that plant protect themselves. Sa phrògram seo, thig Màiri a Ghàrradh Lusan Lògan faisg air an t-Sròn Reamhar – an gàrradh as deòranta an Alba! Seallaidh an Fhear-tasgaidh, Richard Baines, dhith feadhainn dha na lusan a tha fàs a-muigh ann an Lògan a dh’fheumadh an cumail a-staigh an àite sam bith eile an Alba. Thèid iad tro bhog mòr Gunnera mus stad iad airson mocktails air an dèanamh à lusan sa ghàrradh. Innsidh Tèarlach Quinnell dhuinn mu na diofar dhòighean a th’aig lusan iad fhèin a dhìon. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Calum Maclean is on the hunt for a world-famous dish which was created in an Indian restaurant in Glasgow.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Niall Iain Macdonald hosts the quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Standing in the way of our two teams from winning are the ‘Pretenders’, who, from the comfort of their own homes, are on a mission to fox our contestants. Which of this week’s teams, Seumas & Innes or Liz Anne & Eilidh, will get the upper hand and have a chance to take home the grand prize? Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le farpais cheist ùr far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Tha na Mas Fhìoraich a’ gabhail pàirt bhon dachaighean ’s ag amas air a’ chùis a dhèanamh air an dà sgioba. Cò aca bho sgiobaidhean na seachdain-sa, Seumas & Innes no Liz Anne & Eilidh, a gheibh làmh an uachdar agus cothrom fhaighinn air an duais mhòr?

programme.title: Chernobyl – Utopia na Smàl/Chernobyl – Utopia in Flames
programme.desc: Tha a’ chiad readhachtar niùclasach foillsichte san t-saoghal na chunnart dhan t-siostam Sobhieteach air fad. Ach, fiù ’s an dèidh dhaibh sgòth rèidio-beò a lorg os cionn an t-Suain, tha Mosgo a’ fuireach sàmhach. Tha e a’ toirt 36 uairean a thìde an dèidh na mòr-thubaist an riaghaltas innse do dhaoine gum feum iad baile Pripyat, a tha a-nis air a thruailleadh, fhàgail. The world's first exposed nuclear reactor is a danger to the entire Soviet system. However, even after the discovery of a radioactive cloud over Sweden, Moscow continues to remain silent. Then, 36 hours after the catastrophe, the Soviet government finally decides to evacuate the contaminated city of Pripyat. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Tha slighe dùbhlanach aig Somhairle agus a bhràthair Innes air a’ chiad latha aca a’ rothaireachd eadar Inbhir Nis agus Glaschu air an Badger Divide. Somhairle and his brother Innes have a challenging start on their first day cycling between Inverness and Glasgow on the Badger Divide.

programme.title: Alba fon Talamh/Scotland Underground
programme.desc: Calum starts his underground tour in the north west of Scotland. With help from local experts, he explores the incredible cave networks of Applecross. Looking at how man has harnessed underground resources, Calum explores the Nevis Tunnels, the aluminium smelter in Fort William and the globally unique Lochaline sand mine. Tha Calum a’ tòiseachadh air a thuras fon talamh ann an Iar-thuath na h-Alba. Le cuideachadh bho eòlaichean-uamha ionadail, rannsachaidh e lìonraidhean uamhan iongantach na Comraich. Chithear mar a tha mac an duine air feum a dhèanamh de ghoireasan fon talamh fhad ’s a nì Calum rannsachadh air Tunailean Nibheis agus leaghadair aluiminium a’ Ghearasdain, cho math ri mèinne gainmhich ann an Loch Àlainn a tha gun shamhail san t-saoghal. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Fàilte gu Fraochy Bay , baile nach fhaic thu a h-uile là! Is iomadh annas a tha ri fhaicinn sa bhaile , agus sin gun ghuth air cail ach muinntir a bhaile fhèin. Tha cobhair a dhith air dannsairean a bhaile agus 's e Murdo Handel gaisgeach na h uaireach. Welcome to the colourful and unusual world of Fraochy Bay, a miniature metropolis somewhere off the fringes of the map. The local dance troupe are in distress, a situation which calls for careful handling of a musical score.

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Angus Mackay is joined by his daughter Ruth as they go to sea on a spectacular summer's day. Along the way they encounter a large pod of dolphins who take great delight in racing their small boat. Then it’s time for fishing and chat about the formative role of fishing in Ruth’s upbringing. Anns an dàrna prògram mu dheireadh san t-sreath, tha nighean Aonghais, Rut, còmhla ris agus iad aig muir air latha samhraidh eireachdail. Air an t-slighe, coinnichidh iad ri buidheann leumadairean-mara a tha dannsa mun eathar. Às dèidh sin, tha an t-àm ann airson iasgach agus còmhradh mun bhuaidh a bh’ aig iasgach air beatha Ruth.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean à Coats ann am Pàislig, air a lìbhrigeadh le Iain MacFhionghain. Am measg na seinneadairean bidh Costello MacÌomhair, Maeve NicFhionghain agus Seumas Greumach. Cuideachd, an còisir Soisgeul fo stiùir Gareth Fuller. Bidh Iain fhèin a’ meòrachadh air cuspair creideimh le leughadh agus smuain, dàn is seallaidhean spioradail à Tiriodh ann an companachd Dòmhnall Eachann Meek agus bidh Chloe Steele a’ toirt dhuinn seirm adhraidh air a’ phìob à Manachainn nan Lios. Iain MacKinnon presents a mix of hymns, psalms and readings from Coats in Paisley. Amongst the singers performing are Costello Maciver, Maeve MacKinnon and James Graham. Also appearing is the choir Soisgeul conducted by Gareth Fuller. Iain reflects on his own beliefs with a selected reading and thought, spiritual poetry and landscapes from Tiree in the company of Donald E Meek, and Chloe Steele performs a tune of worship on the pipes from Beauly Priory. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

What can Fox and Hare do to cheer Owl up again?

programme.title: Beathaichean a’ Bocadaich
programme.desc: Tha Sophie a’ coimhead tron phrosbaig sheunta aice airson faicinn ciamar a bhios beathaichean a’ bocadaich. Tha i ag ionnsachadh mar a bhios diofar bheathaichean a’ gluasad agus cuide ri a caraidean, tha i a’ cruthachadh dannsa. An-diugh, danns coltach ri ailbhean agus feòrag! Sophie looks through her magic binoculars to find out how animals boogie. She learns how different animals dance and, along with her friends, creates a dance using animal movements. Join her and dance like an elephant and a squirrel!

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air Meaban is Moo gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha i ag iarraidh orra trì rudan òir a lorg. Cha deach gu math dha Meaban a’ lorg òr a-muigh ach saoil am bi ionmhas ri lorg am measg an trealaich sa bhothan? Linda visits Meaban and Moo to set them fun challenges. In this programme, she tasks them with finding three gold items. Meaban has no luck finding gold outside, but perhaps there is treasure to be found amongst the junk in the hut?

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha Bèibidh Dràgon Brot’ mì-thoilichte oir chan fhaod e cluich leis an spàin bhrot’ oir tha ro mhòr dha. Gu fortanach, tha Beag a’ moladh gum faod e taic a thoirt dhaibh-san le bhith toirt am brot air ais dhan uamh – is abair g’eil e taiceil! Baby Soup Dragon is unhappy - he isn’t allowed to play with the soup spoon as it’s too big for him. Fortunately, Small suggests that he can help to deliver the soup instead - and he is hugely helpful!

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha bogsa dìomhaireachd air laighe air a’ phlanaid, le rudan annasach na bhroinn - clobhdan a tha nan tuill cuideachd. Tha e comasach dha na Clangairean siubhal tro na tuill seo - agus abair gu bheil iad trang a’ siubhal! A mysterious box has landed on the planet, with curious things inside it - cloths which are also holes. The Clangers can travel through these holes, and they do it a lot!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Babs Nicgriogair a’ leughadh Eanraig agus an t-Inneal. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Isabelle Marinov, a dhealbhachadh le Olga Shtonda agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Morag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Babs Macgregor reads Eanraig agus an t-Inneal, written by Isabelle Marinov, illustrated by Olga Shtonda and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: ‘S toigh le Valentin a bhith a’ farpais ri seòladairean eile. The e gu tur air a dhòigh air an uisge. ‘S e a mhiann coinneachadh ris a' churaidh, Armel le Cleac’h, seòladair a choisinn mòran dhuaisean aon-neach. Valentin loves to compete with other sailors and be on the water. His dream is to meet his hero, Armel le Cleac’h, a sailor who won a lot of solo trophies.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Nuair a dh’iarr Ivan air Cameron agus Gabriel na caoraich a chur gu fuarach-samhraidh, tha Sebastian 'son aon rud a dhearbhadh - gur e Belle an cù-chaorach as fheàrr a th’ ann! When Cameron and Gabriel are responsible for moving Ivan’s sheep to summer pastures, Sebastian only has one goal, to prove that Belle is the best sheepdog around!

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an tuathanach a' faighinn tiodhlac neo-àbhaisteach bho co-ogha à Astràilia. Mì-thoilichte leis an tiodhlac, tha e a' feuchainn a thilgeil air falbh ach tha e gu daonnan a' tilleadh air ais, dha dhèanamh cinnteach gu bheil comas draoidheachd aig an rud. The Farmer receives a mystery gift from his antipodean cousin. However, he is unimpressed with the present and attempts to throw it away, only for it to keep reappearing. He becomes convinced it has magical powers.

programme.title: Uaine
programme.desc: Thòisich tramaichean a’ ruith ann an Dùn Èideann ann an 2014 agus an-diugh tha faisg air 20,000 duine gan chleachdadh gach latha. The Calum agus a cho-ogha Ruairidh Iain anns a’ bhaile airson barrachd innse dhuinn mun deidhinn. Trams started running in Edinburgh in 2014 and now nearly 20,000 people use them every day. Calum and his cousin Ruairidh Iain visit the city to tell us a bit more about them.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Chan eil na Bògaisean neo na Gumbalan a’ faireachdainn gu math oir tha ’ad a’ fulang le biorgadh bodhaig. Feumar obrachadh le chèile airson leighis a lorg. Saoil am bi e comasach dhaibh seo a dhèanamh? The Bògaisean and the Gumbals are feeling unwell today as they’re suffering from boggle twitches. They must work together to find a cure. Will it be possible?

programme.title: Bus Ghlaschu/Glasgow Bus
programme.desc: Tha seinneadair Lorraine McIntosh à comhlan Deacon Blue eòlach air Bus Ghlaschu. Chi sinn Lorraine dol air ais a Dhùn nan Gall far a bheil ceangal teaghlaich aice. Lorraine MacIntosh, from Deacon Blue, knows the Glasgow bus well. Join the singer as she shares her connections to Donegal.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Claire Macleod from the Isle of Scalpay is Joy’s guest in the studio and Calum Maclean is on the hunt for some important pillars on the Isle of Skye.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Immigration Tracks
programme.desc: From Canada's Eastern province of Cape Breton, we embark on a road-trip east to Toronto, Ontario in search of Scottish Gaelic families who settled in this vast country over 100 years ago. Anne picks up the chanter in the Canadian capital, Ottawa, and goes in search of a relative who once farmed cattle in Bolton, Ontario. How do generations of Canadian Scots identify with their roots? Join Anne McAlpine on a cultural voyage of discovery. An t-seachdains, bidh Anne a’ feuchainn ri port a chluich air an fheadan ann am prìomh bhaile Chanada, Ottawa. Bidh Anne cuideachd a’ dol gu Bolton, Ontario is ceangal-teaghlaich aice ri fear a bha uair a’ cumail chruidh san àite.

programme.title: Am Madadh-Allaidh
programme.desc: The history of the Scottish wolf and its extinction - is it time for their return? Eachdraidh a’mhadaidh-allaidh an Alba, bho chian a bith. A’ bheil an t-am aige tilleadh?

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Shetland’s expansive coastline is home to endless towering cliffs, but its remoteness from the mainland means they see few ascents. With a friend in tow, Coinneach Rankin travels to Shetland in search of new routes and spectacular climbing challenges. Tha oirthir fhada Shealtainn loma làn chreagan tomadach agus seallaidhean nach creidear, ach air sgàth cho cèin ’s a tha i bho thir-mòr, chan fhaigh cus an cothrom sreap ann. Le seann charaid na chuideachd, siubhailidh Coinneach MacFhraing a Shealtainn air tòir slighean ùra is dùbhlain bharraichte. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Leonardo da Vinci (BBC ALBA)
programme.desc: Ann am Florence, Milan, An Ròimh agus mu dheireadh an Fhraing, tha e a’ cur an t-eòlas saidheansail agus ealain an lùib aon de na dealbhan as cliùitiche anns an t-saoghal. In Florence, Milan, Rome and finally France, Leonardo pours the sum of his scientific and artistic knowledge into a portrait that would become the most famous painting ever. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Sreath aithriseach ciùil ùr ann an cuideachd Julie Fowlis agus Muireann NicAmhlaoibh, 's iad air slighe rannsachaidh mu na freumhan aca fhèin, a-nochd ann am Baile Àth-Cliath. Nì Port taisbeanadh air na ceanglaichean dualchais a tha eadar dithis a tha air a bhith na 'n caraidean 's na 'n companaich-ciùil fad iomadh bliadhna. Tha an seinneadair Darren MacIlleathain agus am pìobaire Carole-Ann NicAoidh a' tadhal air grunnd ionadan cliùiteach ann am Baile Àth-Cliath ann an cuideachd Julie is Muireann. Musical documentary with Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh as they take to the road to explore their shared musical roots. In Dublin, Port reveals their shared musical heritage. Port celebrates the common musical heritage of the longtime friends and collaborators as they cross borders and traditions between the west of Ireland and the Western Isles, meeting and playing with friends and musicians en route. Singer Darren MacLean and piper Carole-Anne MacKay join our musical hosts for a tour of several iconic venues. True to form, Dublin doesn't disappoint and gives up some musical gems.

programme.title: Da Vinci: The Lost Treasure
programme.desc: Leonardo da Vinci is considered by many to be one of the greatest artists who ever lived. Yet his reputation rests on only a handful of pictures - including the world's most famous painting, the Mona Lisa. As the National Gallery in London prepares to open its doors on a remarkable exhibition of Leonardo's work, Fiona Bruce travels to Florence, Milan, Paris and Warsaw to uncover the story of this enigmatic genius - and to New York, where she is given an exclusive preview of a sensational discovery: a new Leonardo.

programme.title: A History of Britain by Simon Schama
programme.desc: Simon Schama examines the turbulent years in Britain from 1649 to 1689, from Oliver Cromwell's republic to Charles II's restoration and James II's subsequent pro-Catholic rule from which he was quickly deposed. This is the dramatic story of the revolutionary period after the execution of Charles I, when Cromwell ruled with an iron hand and Charles II attempted to restore the lustre of the monarchy.

programme.title: Scotland's Finest: The Story of the Highland Games
programme.desc: A journey into the history, pageantry and characters that have shaped a Scottish phenomenon. Acclaimed actor Bill Paterson narrates the astonishing story of the Highland Games. From the battling clans to Queen Victoria's infatuation with her Highland subjects, the games have become a symbol of community and identity in Scotland and all across the world.

programme.title: Genius of the Ancient World
programme.desc: In the final episode, Bettany travels to China on the trail of Confucius, a great sage of Chinese history whose ideas have fundamentally shaped the country of his birth for around 2,500 years.

programme.title: Lost Cities of the Ancients
programme.desc: In the Lambeyeque valley in northern Peru lies a strange lost world - the forgotten ruins of 250 mysterious pyramids, including some of the biggest on the planet, colossal structures made out of mud bricks. Long ago, the Lambeyeque people were haunted by a terrible fear and believed that building pyramids was essential to their survival. Their obsession reached its height at a city called Tucume, an eerie place of 26 pyramids standing side by side, the last pyramids this civilisation created before they vanished forever. What was the fear that drove these people to build so many pyramids, what were they for and why did the whole civilisation suddenly vanish? This film captures the moments when archaeologists at the site uncovered a mass of bodies of human sacrifice victims, following a trail of clues into the dark story of Tucume. It recreates the strange rituals of the people of the valley, revealing a civilisation whose obsession to build pyramids eventually turned to horror, until Tucume finally vanished in a bloody frenzy of human sacrifice.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Acclaimed screenwriter Stephen Poliakoff shares his memories of the BBC's 1980 television drama Caught on a Train, his Bafta award-winning collaboration with celebrated producer Kenith Trodd. The drama was based on a real-life encounter Stephen experienced with an angry fellow passenger on a train trip across Europe. It stars the legendary Dame Peggy Ashcroft and Michael Kitchen as strangers who clash at the start of their journey but come to an understanding by the time they reach their destination. Here, Stephen reveals how the production came together, why he was left thinking the drama may herald the end of his career, and which iconic James Bond villainess was almost cast as the leading lady.

programme.title: How to Get Ahead
programme.desc: Writer, broadcaster and Newsnight arts correspondent Stephen Smith explores Renaissance Florence under the reign of Grand Duke Cosimo Medici. Cosimo's fledgling court prized the finer things in life and some of the greatest painters, sculptors and craftsmen in world history came to serve the Grand Duke. But successful courtiers had to have brains as well as brawn. The canniest of them looked to theorists like Niccolo Machiavelli for underhand ways to get ahead, whilst enlightened polymaths turned their minds to the heavens, and to ice cream.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Water has been a flashpoint in the Middle East and worldwide demand is outstripping supply, so how do we make sure there's enough to go round? This most basic resource is vital for drinking, sanitation and agriculture, but also for jobs and economies everywhere. The World Bank's global director for water Saroj Kumar Jha explains why they're trying to make it more of a priority for government spending. And Mareen Schneider, the founder and CEO of project developer Grasshopper Investments, explains how she's coming up with radical new ways for the private sector to invest in water. Plus, Ben Thompson also hears from José Manuel Entrecanales, the CEO of Spanish infrastructure giant Acciona, about the projects they're building around the world and why we need to rethink the value we give to water.

programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate the fraudulent websites convincing shoppers to invest in a ‘best-buy’ home appliance – and meet the woman who learned too late that her top-rated dehumidifier wasn’t up to the job. At the advice clinic in Mansfield, experts step in to help the couple denied boarding when their passports went missing at the airport. And in another how-to guide, consumer expert Harry Kind explains the steps to take when you’ve been involved in a collision on the road.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in Wales, where a mixed commercial and residential unit is in surprisingly good condition. Jacqui’s house in Norwich is in similarly decent nick. But are they hiding any secret issues? Dion is in Staffordshire, where a three-bedroom mid-terrace has a quirky layout to contend with.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles heads to Sussex, where experts Raj Bisram and Nick Hall join the teams as they search for the best items to sell at auction in Newbury. Eric also sails along the Kennet and Avon Canal to learn about its fascinating 200-year history.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In this episode, the team try to prevent a barber in Doncaster, who is actually working whilst on the phone, paying out to a tricksy scammer. As the scammer tries to persuade her that he is there to help recover some lost cryptocurrency, the ground team are on the road to her shop to put a stop to the scam. The team have their work cut out to persuade the barber and her colleagues that they are legit – and this particular race against time goes right to the wire.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Giant Sea Monster
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough investigates the discovery of a lifetime: the giant skull of a prehistoric sea monster, known as a pliosaur – the Tyrannosaurus rex of the seas!

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In true Escape to the Country style, today’s couple (both former international rugby players) want to leave London in search of a rural idyll in Dorset, and Alistair Appleton is the man to help them on their way. Aside from property, Alistair learns about the health benefits of watercress at a farm which specialises in growing this delicious and nutritious crop.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, flatmates Rachel, Scott, Tara and Daniel – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The devoted owners of no fewer than six Irish wolfhounds are in desperate need of more space for them and those countless muddy paws, so have set their sights on Suffolk for a bit more elbow room. Briony May Williams is there to guide them as they tour a selection of beautiful homes. Briony also gets to mess about on a stunning million pound, bespoke wooden yacht, a sister vessel to the ones featured in James Bond.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Morning Live

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The devoted owners of no fewer than six Irish wolfhounds are in desperate need of more space for them and those countless muddy paws, so have set their sights on Suffolk for a bit more elbow room. Briony May Williams is there to guide them as they tour a selection of beautiful homes. Briony also gets to mess about on a stunning million pound, bespoke wooden yacht, a sister vessel to the ones featured in James Bond.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The devoted owners of no fewer than six Irish wolfhounds are in desperate need of more space for them and those countless muddy paws, so have set their sights on Suffolk for a bit more elbow room. Briony May Williams is there to guide them as they tour a selection of beautiful homes. Briony also gets to mess about on a stunning million pound, bespoke wooden yacht, a sister vessel to the ones featured in James Bond.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring comedian and actor Phil Wang, dating expert Anna Williamson, actor and comedian Miles Jupp and actor Jamie-Lee O’Donnell as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Acting on a tip off, the Peelers storm a city centre flat on a drugs bust. Inside, a startled suspect is immediately cuffed and arrested while outside, the PSNI team search the nearby streets for the suspected big-time dealer they think may have fled the scene with more drugs. On Great Victoria Street in Belfast city centre, police attempt to arrest a man who refuses to comply with a search. The situation quickly escalates and he is detained by a number of officers who use a spit guard and leg restraints. The man is taken into custody where he continues to kick off. Officers and custody staff surround the man in his cell as they try to get him under control. Later, Stephen interviews the Deputy Chief Constable, Bobby Singleton, and questions him about some PSNI tactics and officers’ use of force.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The devoted owners of no fewer than six Irish wolfhounds are in desperate need of more space for them and those countless muddy paws, so have set their sights on Suffolk for a bit more elbow room. Briony May Williams is there to guide them as they tour a selection of beautiful homes. Briony also gets to mess about on a stunning million pound, bespoke wooden yacht, a sister vessel to the ones featured in James Bond.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon

Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring comedian and actor Phil Wang, dating expert Anna Williamson, actor and comedian Miles Jupp and actor Jamie-Lee O’Donnell as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon

Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon

programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The devoted owners of no fewer than six Irish wolfhounds are in desperate need of more space for them and those countless muddy paws, so have set their sights on Suffolk for a bit more elbow room. Briony May Williams is there to guide them as they tour a selection of beautiful homes. Briony also gets to mess about on a stunning million pound, bespoke wooden yacht, a sister vessel to the ones featured in James Bond.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.
